messages:
emily: Hey team, customer (AcmeHealth) reporting sharp spike in latency + 401s from EU users since ~09:10 UTC. They say requests resolve to a us-west IP and tokens look valid. Can we triage?

samir: ack — oncall looking. Any quick repro from customer? headers, dig, curl?

emily: customer posted dig + curl, pasted below.

emily: ```
$ dig +short inference.redwood.com
54.175.23.10

$ dig +short inference.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
54.175.23.10

$ curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://inference.redwood.com/v1/generate
> HTTP/2 401
> x-region: us-west-2
> x-request-id: req_abc123
{
  "error": "invalid_token"
}
```

emily: They also included a trace showing latency 1800ms for initial TCP to 54.175.23.10.

netbot: alert: dns-geolocation-shift detected for customer AcmeHealth — queries resolving to us-west from EU ASN 12345 since 09:08 UTC. TTL on answers: 300s.

alex: thanks. initial suspicion: resolver is returning US-pop IP because EDNS client subnet not present / ISP NAT64 or HTTP proxy rewriting source. If geoip sees client IP as US, it routes to us-west and our routing policy falls back to US model causing auth token region check mismatch.

maya: also possible: our prefix affinity cache on the edge still has warm entries mapping that IP to us-west; when tokens are scoped to eu region we return 401. Need traceroute from customer + dig + EDNS details.

emily: customer sent traceroute too: ```
traceroute to inference.redwood.com (54.175.23.10), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  12.3 ms
 3  isp-proxy.example.net  30.4 ms
 4  54.175.23.10  240.7 ms
```

samir: hop 3 looks like ISP proxy. Ask customer to run `dig +edns=0 +noedns` and `dig +edns=1 +subnet=0.0.0.0/0` or `dig +short +norecurse` to check EDNS.

emily: customer ran: ```
$ dig inference.redwood.com +noedns +short
54.175.23.10

$ dig inference.redwood.com +subnet=1.2.3.4/32 +short
54.175.23.10
```

emily: they say their corporate NAT strips ECS.

alex: confirms: if ECS stripped, geoip lookup uses NAT IP which is served from US. Two work items: 1) workaround in product to accept cross-region tokens when region_hint provided, 2) operational: reduce TTLs for affected pop and trigger cache prefill/probes.

maya: quick mitigation: customer can set header `x-region-hint: eu-west-1` or pass query param region=eu to override routing now. We can also add temporary tolerant auth check for this customer while we investigate.

lisa: I messaged the customer with the header workaround and asked for permission to enable tolerant auth. They approved.

alex: technical plan:
- create probe to query from EU public resolvers (ASN 12345) to reproduce and validate.
- push small routing preference tweak to prefer eu-backed model if origin ASN in our edge affinity list.
- reduce DNS TTL for inference.redwood.com on affected edge to 60s for 6 hours.
- coord with CDN vendor (cc @eng-net) to prewarm eu IPs and invalidate relevant caches.

samir: I've opened INC-2026 and assigned eng-net + eng-runtime. Adding priority P1 because customer billing/latency impacted.

netbot: incident INC-2026 created by samir.

emily: notes for support: customer reported billing spike because requests retried to different region; finance FYI.

maya: follow-up: we'll run a small probe matrix (EDNS present/absent, with/without region header) and post results. I suspect ~70% of their office proxies strip ECS which explains intermittent nature.

alex: longer-term: consider offering a token-scoping policy that accepts region claims signed by the token issuer to avoid 401s during routing mismatches. Also add telemetry to flag resolver ECS-stripping ASNs.

lisa: Customer confirmed latency improved after header workaround and we enabled tolerant auth for 2 hours. They will monitor and report regressions.

samir: action items:
1) eng-net: run DNS + ECS probe for ASN 12345 (due in 1h)
2) eng-runtime: implement temporary routing override for customer (due 2h)
3) support: follow up with customer and collect 3 more traceroutes from different office locations (due 30m)
4) finance: track any invoice anomalies (FYI)

emily: tagging this thread for postmortem if we see recurrence. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
